response_text: In the simulator, every synthetic invoice carries a deterministic correct answer for free. That stops being true once real invoices arrive — nobody hands the system the right answer up front. ADR-0009's answer is post-hoc audit sampling: a slice of an agent's decisions gets pulled for human review after the fact, at a rate that shrinks as the agent climbs the ladder (100% reviewed at the floor rung, down to 5% at the top). Those reviewed samples become the accuracy evidence the trust score is built from. It's also why the Wilson lower bound matters more, not less, at high trust — the reviewed sample shrinks even as the agent's raw decision volume keeps growing, so the confidence interval has to correctly widen around a smaller, sampled n rather than the system quietly trusting a number it can no longer fully verify.
